text: Simvastatin reduces CD40 expression in an experimental model of early saphenous vein graft (VG) arterialization. Saphenous vein and internal mammary artery (IMA) samples from 16 patients not on statins underwent pulsatile pressure distension and culture with or without Simvastatin (Merck Sharp & Dohme). CD40 was significantly lower in IMA than in distended and non-distended VG. Pressure distension upregulated CD40 in VG segments at 24 and 48 h. Simvastatin significantly reduced CD40 in both venous and arterial samples (P < 0.001 each); the effect was unaffected by L-NAME but reversed by mevalonic acid. Mean soluble CD40L (sCD40L) in culture supernatants rose over time, indicating the vessel wall—not only platelets—is a source of CD40/sCD40L. Simvastatin modulates endothelial CD40–sCD40L in venous and arterial grafts, suggesting a pharmacological tool against graft failure.
